title: What is NPM?
overview: NPM (Node Package Manager) is the default package manager for Node.js. It allows developers to install, manage, and share JavaScript packages.

example.title: NPM Purpose
example.content:
✔ Install packages
✔ Manage dependencies
✔ Run scripts
✔ Share packages

title: Understanding package.json
overview: The package.json file contains project information, scripts, dependencies, and configuration required for a Node.js project.

title: Installing Packages
overview: NPM allows developers to install external packages that provide additional functionality to applications.

title: Dependencies and DevDependencies
overview: Dependencies are packages required for application execution, while devDependencies are used only during development.

example.title: Dependency Types
example.content:
dependencies → Required in production

devDependencies → Development tools

title: NPM Scripts
overview: NPM scripts allow developers to create shortcuts for frequently used commands like starting applications or running tests.

title: Topic Summary
overview: You learned how NPM manages packages, dependencies, project configuration, and automation scripts in Node.js applications.

example.title: Quick Revision
example.content:
✔ NPM manages packages.
✔ package.json stores project details.
✔ npm install adds packages.
✔ Scripts automate commands.
